blockbuilder.visual_critic_note: Deliberate monochromatic palette (#4477AA on dark), uppercase panel labels with letter-spacing, and coherent dark-theme layout show real design intent, but the color scatter panel renders too dim (many points invisible against the dark background), the force graph labels are barely legible at 9px, and the overall layout is too compact to breathe.
blockbuilder.encoding_integrity_note: Strong encoding integrity: scaleSqrt used correctly for node and color-dot size, bar chart has zero baseline with data-driven y-domain, hue/lightness axes use semantically fixed [0,360]/[0,100] domains (not deceptive), and timeline y-scale is frozen to full-data max so filtered views have stable axes — minor gap is absent key functions in data joins, creating permutation-relation fragility if data ever updates in place.
blockbuilder.stress_test_note: Dirty-flag + RAF pattern correctly defers all canvas/DOM rendering, but bitFilter.set() iterates all 34K blocks synchronously on every brush mousemove (no throttle), and the full el.innerHTML rebuild of 200 rows also runs every RAF tick — expensive computation is not deferred, only the draw calls are.
blockbuilder.cognitive_load_note: Four-view crossfilter stays within working memory limits, the pre-simulated (stopped) force layout avoids reheat animation chaos, and the monochromatic network palette keeps 60 nodes readable — but the color scatter's HCL encoding (dot-is-its-own-color plotted on hue/lightness axes) requires a moment of inference that adds unnecessary cognitive cost for first-time viewers.
